title: How we walk: the third law (হাঁটা ও নিউটনের তৃতীয় সূত্র)
placement: Book page 86, topic 3.8 (example): how we walk. Next to চিত্র ৩.১২ (a person's foot pushing the ground back, the ground pushing the person forward, labelled F and −F).
description: Interactive 3D figure for how we walk (হাঁটা), the example that explains Newton's third law (নিউটনের তৃতীয় সূত্র), book page 86, topic 3.8, next to চিত্র ৩.১২. A student stands on a path, seen from the side, real size. One big numbered action ("শক্ত মাটিতে পা দিয়ে ধাক্কা দাও", its badge rings the pushing foot; a tap on the student works too) takes the first push-off of a walk, slowed down 4 times, and holds at the telling moment with a pause note. Everyday words first, one verb (ধাক্কা): an orange arrow lying on the ground behind the foot says "পা মাটিকে ধাক্কা দিচ্ছে" and a crimson arrow at the shoe pointing forward says "মাটি মানুষটিকে ধাক্কা দিচ্ছে", the two equally long on one scale (100 N = 0.7 m); the student has moved off from a dashed start line. The panel is the clean sheet: the page's three grounds as one row of words (শক্ত মাটি, ঝুরঝুরে বালু, পিচ্ছিল মেঝে), each with its push under it once tried, the action going on to the next ground; one result line ("পা মাটিকে ধাক্কা দিল, মাটি মানুষটিকে ধাক্কা দিল। দুটি ধাক্কাই সমান, যেমন ১০০ নিউটন"; the numbers are an example); one short rule per idea in plain words ("শক্ত মাটিতে পা আটকে থাকে। পা মাটিকে পেছনে, মাটি আমাদের সামনে ধাক্কা দেয়"; "বালু সরে যায়"; "ঘর্ষণ খুব কম, তাই পা পিছলে যায়"), the current ground's own line always staying, and the book's own sentence under it last, once all three grounds are found ("বল প্রয়োগ করলে বিপরীত এবং সমান বল পাওয়া যায়"), when the two pushes also get the book's names F and −F on their labels. Firm ground: both pushes 100 N (a = 2 ms⁻², the student moves off at 1.2 m/s); loose sand: the sand gives way, a heap is pushed back, both 50 N; a floor made slippery with soapy water or oil: the foot slides back, both only 20 N, the student hardly moves. The book's slanted arrows are drawn as their horizontal parts only. Numbers are for an example 50 kg student (the book gives none). Test tab: 5 questions on held scenes in the same plain words, the cause left out so the picture has to be read (which arrow moves the student, how big the ground's push is, why equal and opposite pushes do not cancel, why the student hardly moves on the slippery floor, who pushes the student forward), each wrong answer with its note. Phone-first, Bangla.
